signals.signal: FY2025 annual operating report (published inside the audited separate financial statements PDF) discloses the self-service fleet for the first time: on average 680,000 customers/month used cash withdrawal across 434 devices, of which 375 dispense RSD; almost 21 million ATM cash-withdrawal transactions in 2025 including 442,000 in EUR.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Pojedinacni finansijski izvestaji 2025 (incl. Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025)
signals.implies: First primary-source fleet count since 2024 vintage data. 434 devices with only 375 RSD-dispensing implies ~59 units that are non-RSD or deposit-only - a gap Printec can address with multi-currency recyclers plus managed services.
signals.likelihood: Fleet refresh continues; contract-driven replacement already underway
signals.followup: Reconcile 434 vs the 2024-vintage 407 ATMs / 110 cash-in / 118 kiosks; ask whether 434 includes the 122 Payten-owned external units.

signals.signal: FY2025 report: 123 multifunctional cash-in/cash-out self-service devices installed over the last five years (RSD deposit/withdrawal plus EUR transactions from FX payment accounts). RSD deposits at devices now 86% of equivalent teller deposits (~120,000 customers/month); EUR deposits 73% device-migrated (~30,000 customers/month). Volumes 2025: 1.5m RSD deposits (+13.8%) worth almost RSD 56bn (+21.4%), and 386,000 EUR deposits (+18.6%) worth almost EUR 360m (+21.4%).
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: Proven, quantified recycler business case at the #1 Serbian bank - direct fit for Printec cash automation/recyclers and cash-cycle managed services; 123 of 434 devices are multifunctional, so ~70% of the fleet is still cash-out only.
signals.likelihood: High - migration targets already met, expansion explicitly continuing
signals.followup: Identify OEM of the 123 multifunctional units (Diebold Nixdorf Cineo per Payten 2020/2023 releases) and the replacement cadence.

signals.signal: FY2025 report: a separate corporate/entrepreneur initiative deployed 135 specialised daily-takings (pazar) deposit devices across 123 branches; 86% of network-wide merchant takings deposits migrated from the teller (~195,000 deposits/month), rising to ~87% in branches that have a device. 2025 volume: 2.3m takings deposits worth almost RSD 315bn.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: A 135-unit merchant cash-deposit estate across 123 of 134 branches - a distinct, sizeable Printec cash-automation/CDM fleet with its own refresh cycle, plus SLA-based managed services and cash-in-transit integration.
signals.likelihood: Refresh/expansion likely as 11 branches still uncovered
signals.followup: Name the OEM of the 135 takings devices - not disclosed; likely distinct from the ATM fleet.

signals.signal: FY2025 report: ATM network expanded by 14 new devices during 2025 while 26 in-branch (internal) ATMs were replaced. Branch count held flat at 134 but restructured into 66 clusters; network FTE cut to 1,336 (-26 vs 2024); cashless-format branches rose to 24% of the network; 6 branches fully refurbished and 20 partially adapted.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: A running ~40 device/year in-branch replacement + expansion cadence, and a cashless-branch conversion programme at 24% with headroom to grow - both direct Printec self-service hardware + branch-transformation opportunities.
signals.followup: Confirm whether the 26 internal replacements were Diebold Nixdorf Cineo and who supplied/installed them (Payten scope is external locations).

signals.signal: CORRECTION to baseline: the '200 ATMs replaced with Diebold Nixdorf Cineo incl. recycling' story is a Payten release dated 04/03/2020, NOT part of the 2023 outsourcing. The separate ATM-outsourcing deal is dated 13/12/2023: Payten bought 122 ATMs at Banca Intesa external locations under a 36-month contract, undertaking to replace all installed machines with latest-generation Diebold Nixdorf CashOut and Recycling devices within the first 12 months, plus pre-installation works, network communications, Vynamic Security suite, site-lease negotiation and all ATM operational duties; the bank moves to a no-investment, fixed-cost model and transfers VISA/Mastercard/PCI DSS compliance risk to Payten.
signals.source_name: Payten - 'Banca Intesa a.d. Belgrade ATM outsourcing' and 'Banca Intesa Strengthens its ATM Network Supported by Payten'
signals.implies: A 36-month term from Dec-2023 puts contract expiry around Dec-2026 - a live re-tender window for ATM-as-a-service, and the single most actionable Printec managed-services entry point at this bank.
signals.followup: Verify the 36-month term end date and whether it auto-renews; watch ASEE/Payten investor releases and any Banca Intesa procurement notice in H2-2026.

signals.signal: FY2025 audited note on right-of-use assets confirms the bank leases POS terminals and ancillary devices, ATM and ATS printer devices, recognised using a portfolio approach - i.e. the self-service and POS estate is held off-balance-sheet as an operating lease rather than owned.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Napomene uz pojedinacne finansijske izvestaje za 2025, Note 20(a)
signals.implies: The bank has institutionalised a device-as-a-service commercial model for both ATMs and POS - Printec should bid opex/managed-service structures, not capex sales, and the POS estate is also leased and therefore contestable.
signals.likelihood: Structural; applies to any future bid
signals.followup: Extract the RSD value of equipment right-of-use assets and lease liabilities to size the annual device spend.

signals.signal: FY2025 strategy section commits to strengthening governance and internal controls 'through enhanced non-financial risk management and digitalisation of processes in financial-crime prevention and compliance', to reduce operational losses. AML is embedded as a Risk Appetite Framework metric and in 2025 new early-warning limits were introduced specifically to manage AML risk, legal risk and IT risk. AML training totalled 23,130 hours; an AML Academy runs internally.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: An explicit, budgeted programme to digitalise financial-crime prevention - direct fit for Printec AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring, and the clearest stated software need in the whole report.
signals.followup: Establish whether the AML/transaction-monitoring platform is an ISP group mandate or a local buy - decisive for whether Printec can bid.

signals.entity: Banca Intesa Beograd / Intesa Sanpaolo Group
signals.signal: FY2025 strategy names the implementation of the 'Isytech International IBD solution' to support business-model transformation, delivering digital-channel platforms and a single work environment integrating physical and digital branch operations into one sales-and-service environment; plus a marketing-automation platform for CRM/data, and wealth/insurance and credit platforms. Separately the bank commits to 'centralise or outsource shared activities to achieve scalability', and to a next-generation-procurement cost-optimisation transformation programme.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025, section 5 (Elementi strategije)
signals.implies: Core digital-channel and branch-workstation stack is an ISP group standard (Isytech/IBD) and therefore largely closed to Printec; but the explicit intent to outsource shared activities and to run next-gen procurement is a positive signal for Printec managed services around cash, self-service and POS.
signals.followup: Map which layers ISP mandates centrally (channels, core, AML) vs which stay local (device estate, cash logistics, POS acquiring hardware).

signals.signal: FY2025 report: contactless ATM cash withdrawal reached 1 million transactions in 2025 from 101,000 unique users, with December alone above 160,000 transactions and 55,000 users, growth explicitly attributed to the rising number of contactless-capable ATMs.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: Contactless capability is not yet universal across the 434 devices - a concrete functional gap driving further replacement, favouring modern NFC-equipped recyclers.
signals.followup: Determine how many of the 434 devices are contactless-capable today.

signals.signal: FY2025 report: Paperless Branch pilot started May-2025 for KYC questionnaires, account-opening forms and cash loans; after the pilot the paperless cash-loan process was extended to the entire sales network in August-2025, reaching 36.9% of all cash loans disbursed in December-2025. A Remote Offer channel lets customers review, accept and sign full documentation in the mobile app using a qualified electronic certificate. Production rollout for overdrafts and term deposits planned for early 2026.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: Live digital onboarding / eKYC / e-signature programme with an expanding product scope - a Printec digital-onboarding/eKYC adjacency, though the platform choice appears already made.
signals.followup: Identify the e-signature/eKYC vendor behind Paperless Branch and Remote Offer - not disclosed.

signals.signal: FY2025 report: fraud/financial-crime operations sit in a dedicated Cyber Security, Fraud Prevention and BCM department with a standing Monitoring Team for suspicious payment transactions; in 2025 it analysed 168 suspected abuse cases of which 153 were proven (4 internal, 149 external). 2,611 employees took anti-bribery and AML training totalling 23,130 hours. The bank's anti-corruption guideline was updated to follow the revised 'ISP Group Anti Corruption Guidelines'.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025 (in audited FS PDF)
signals.implies: A live, staffed transaction-monitoring function with measurable case volume - the natural buying centre for Printec transaction monitoring / fraud analytics, though group policy sets the framework.
signals.likelihood: Ongoing; digitalisation of the function is a stated 2026 priority
signals.followup: Find out whether the payment-transaction monitoring engine is ISP-mandated or locally procured.

signals.signal: FY2025 operational-risk disclosure lists 'third-party events (vendors, suppliers and outsourcers)' as a monitored operational-risk indicator, and the ICT & security risk self-assessment explicitly covers 'entrusting to third parties'. The RAF sets a zero-tolerance hard limit for any single large operational-risk event.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025, section 10 (Sistem upravljanja rizicima)
signals.implies: Any Printec managed-services bid will be assessed under formal outsourcing/ICT third-party risk governance - proposals must lead with SLAs, PCI DSS, business-continuity and incident evidence, not price.
signals.followup: Obtain the bank's outsourcing due-diligence questionnaire ahead of any ATM-as-a-service re-tender.

signals.entity: Banca Intesa Beograd / Serbian eGovernment Office
signals.signal: Banca Intesa was first in the Serbian market to launch a fully paperless branch process and remote offer using a cloud qualified electronic signature; signing is performed through the state ConsentID mobile application, in cooperation with the Office for IT and eGovernment, with activation parameters issued digitally inside the Intesa Mobi app.
signals.source_name: Biznis i Finansije (bif.rs) - 'Banca Intesa prva na trzistu uvela bespapirni proces i ponudu na daljinu uz kvalifikovani elektronski potpis'
signals.implies: The e-signature/eKYC layer is state-provided (ConsentID), so Printec digital-onboarding/eKYC white space at this bank is largely closed; any play must be integration/orchestration around ConsentID rather than a competing signature product.
signals.followup: Check whether other Serbian banks are also standardising on ConsentID - if so it is a market-wide constraint on eKYC vendors.

signals.signal: NBS quarterly payment-services review for Q1-2026 (published June 2026): acceptance network expanded to 187,957 POS terminals, +10.3% / +17,523 devices YoY; virtual points of sale +20.2%; the NUMBER OF ATMs GREW 3.6% YoY. 195,192,834 card transactions at Serbian points of sale (+18.7%); 13,343,642 payment cards issued (+8.0%); mobile-banking users 5,337,237 (+10.3%).
signals.source_name: Narodna banka Srbije, Pregled podataka u vezi s pruzanjem platnih usluga i izdavanjem elektronskog novca za prvo tromesecje 2026
signals.implies: Serbia's ATM estate is still GROWING (+3.6%) while Western European fleets shrink, and POS added 17,523 units in a year - a genuinely expanding hardware+services market for Printec self-service and POS, not a replacement-only market.
signals.followup: Pull the same table for Q2-2026 when published to confirm the ATM growth rate and get the absolute ATM count.

signals.signal: NBS published in June 2026 a draft of amendments to the Law on Interbank Fees and Special Rules for Card-Based Payment Transactions which for the first time caps interchange on cards issued by banks ABROAD when used for payments in Serbia, at 0.2% of transaction value for debit and 0.3% for credit - the same caps that have applied to domestically issued cards since end-2018. Domestic points of sale and internet merchants are in scope.
signals.source_name: N1 / Biznis i Finansije reporting on the NBS draft law
signals.implies: Compresses acquiring economics on the fast-growing foreign-tourist card volume, pushing acquirers toward volume and lower cost-to-serve - favours Printec POS estate managed services and terminal-fleet efficiency plays over margin-funded hardware.
signals.likelihood: Draft stage; adoption plausible within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Locate the draft text and public-consultation deadline on nbs.rs - only press coverage was found, the NBS primary page was not located this run.

signals.signal: NBS AML regulations page (re-verified this run against the primary regulator source) flags TWO items as NOVO: the Decision on guidelines for applying the AML/CFT Law for NBS-supervised obliged entities, Official Gazette 41/2025 (replacing the 13/2018-49/2021 version), and the Decision on conditions and manner of establishing and verifying the identity of a natural person using means of electronic communication, Official Gazette 43/2026 (replacing the 15/2019, 84/2020, 49/2021 version).
signals.source_name: Narodna banka Srbije - Propisi iz oblasti sprecavanja pranja novca
signals.implies: A refreshed remote-identification rulebook forces every Serbian bank to revisit its video/eID onboarding controls in 2026 - a compliance-driven trigger for Printec eKYC and AML/compliance tooling across the whole market, not just Intesa.
signals.followup: Read the 43/2026 text for the specific technical requirements (liveness, recording, retention) that create product gaps.

signals.signal: On the ASEE H1-2026 earnings call the CEO said of the ATM business that 'we will finance all of the outsourced things with debt' and that the group will be 'more disciplined in leveraging this business'. ASEE's FY2023 annual report separately records that Serbia was the main source of WEAKER ATM-line revenues, caused by lower hardware deliveries and only partly offset by growth in own maintenance services, and that capex for outsourcing infrastructure and independent ATM networks is the one category not financed from own funds.
signals.source_name: Investing.com transcript of ASEE H1 2026 earnings call; ASEE Group Annual Report for the year ended 31 December 2023
signals.implies: The incumbent is signalling balance-sheet discipline on debt-financed ATM-as-a-service just as the Banca Intesa 36-month contract reaches its window - the clearest opening for Printec to bid a competing managed-service model.
signals.likelihood: Constraint is stated policy; effect on renewal unproven
signals.followup: Obtain the ASEE FY2025 management report (not located this run) and the full H1-2026 transcript for ATM-outsourcing capex and contract-pipeline commentary.

signals.signal: FY2025 report: the bank rebuilt its PD, LGD and EAD credit models on a new Analytics Lab platform using Google Cloud BigQuery and Vertex AI, with all algorithms in Python; the PD model was delivered to the parent bank for review with validation and implementation planned for H1-2026, and EAD/LGD finalisation for Q2-2026. Historical default-definition reconstruction for legal entities continues into Q1-2026.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd, Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025
signals.implies: Analytics and risk-model workloads are on Google Cloud under parent-bank governance - mirrors UniCredit Bulbank and UniCredit RO, and means any Printec analytics/AML offering must integrate with GCP rather than propose a separate stack.
signals.followup: Check whether financial-crime analytics is also being moved onto the same Vertex AI platform, as at UniCredit Bulbank.

signals.signal: FY2025 confirms market leadership: assets RSD 1,073.25bn, 15.32% market share, #1 in Serbia; operating income RSD 60,693.32m (+11.75%); net profit RSD 31,048.29m (+15.85%); 134 branches in 4 regional centres and 2,943 employees at 31/12/2025 (3,044 at 31/12/2024). Named best bank in Serbia by Euromoney for 2026 (its ninth), with digitalisation and distribution channels explicitly weighted in the assessment.
signals.source_name: Banca Intesa a.d. Beograd audited separate financial statements 2025; Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026 as reported by Bloomberg Adria
signals.implies: Headcount fell ~3.3% while the branch count held flat - the efficiency gains are coming from device migration, which validates the self-service and cash-automation investment case Printec should lead with.

coverage_notes: Fresh run, no checkpoint existed. PRIMARY BREAKTHROUGH: the FY2025 narrative annual report (Godisnji izvestaj o poslovanju za 2025) IS published but only as an appendix inside the audited separate financial statements PDF - the standalone Godisnji_izvestaj_2025 path 404s and the listing page renders via JS with no PDF links. Downloaded the 5.29 MB FS PDF and extracted text locally with pdfminer, which closes the baseline's '2025 narrative annual report unpublished' gap and supplies first-party 2025 fleet figures (434 devices / 375 RSD-dispensing / 123 multifunctional / 135 merchant takings devices / +14 new ATMs / 26 internal replacements), superseding the 2024-vintage 407 ATM / 110 cash-in / 118 kiosk numbers. Also CORRECTED the baseline's conflation of two separate Payten events: the '200 ATMs replaced with DN Cineo incl. recycling' release is dated 04/03/2020, while the 122-ATM buy-out / 36-month outsourcing deal is dated 13/12/2023 - implying a contract window around Dec-2026. Angles used: (1) bank primary IR/PDF path-probing with a desktop UA plus local PDF text extraction; (2) vendor primary sources (Payten Serbia and the Payten/ISP Bosnia release, ASEE group annual report and H1-2026 earnings call - a source environment not used in prior runs); (3) NBS regulator primary - payment-services quarterly PDF for Q1-2026 and the AML regulations register, both fetched with a desktop UA; (4) Serbian-language business press (bif.rs, Bloomberg Adria, N1) for the interchange draft law and the paperless/ConsentID launch. GENUINE GAPS: the OEM of the 123 multifunctional devices and the 135 merchant takings devices is nowhere disclosed - Diebold Nixdorf Cineo remains a strong inference from the 2020 and 2023 Payten releases but is NOT confirmed for 2025 deployments; whether the 434 devices include the 122 Payten-owned external units is unclear; the exact expiry date and renewal mechanics of the 36-month Payten contract are undisclosed by both parties; the ASEE FY2025 management report was not located (only FY2023 and FY2018 PDFs resolved); no absolute national ATM count was obtainable because the NBS acceptance-network XLS is a legacy file last saved in 2018 and only the percentage change appears in the Q1-2026 PDF; and no procurement/tender notices exist because Banca Intesa is a private bank outside the Serbian public-procurement portal.
access_issues: bancaintesa.rs/en/o-nama/investitori/publikacije.html -> 404. The annual-report listing page (bancaintesa.rs/stanovnistvo/finansijski-izvestaji/godisnji-izvestaji.html) returns 200 but renders its document list via JS, exposing no PDF hrefs to curl; guessed Godisnji_izvestaj_2025 path -> 404. Worked around by probing the audited-FS path, which returned 200 (5.29 MB), then extracting text locally with pdfminer - the narrative report is inside it. Bank ATM/branch locator exposes no JSON API; /.rest/* probes returned 302 redirects, so no live fleet count could be scraped. nbs.rs pages returned 200 with a desktop User-Agent (no 403 encountered this run); NBS payment-statistics XLS files parsed only partially because pandas/xlrd are unavailable in this environment AND the acceptance-network XLS is a legacy file last saved 06/03/2018 - used the Q1-2026 PDF instead, extracted with pdfminer. see.asseco.com/news/... 301-redirects to asee.io which then returns 404 for the Banca Intesa self-service-branch article - that source is lost, logged rather than dropped. Two guessed ASEE FY2025 report URLs returned 404 or resolved to the FY2018/FY2023 documents.
operator_requests: 1) ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe management report for FY2025 and the full H1-2026 earnings-call transcript - needed for ATM-outsourcing capex, the Serbian ATM contract pipeline and any comment on the Banca Intesa renewal; the FY2025 PDF was not resolvable from asee.io this run. 2) The NBS draft amendments to the Law on Interbank Fees (published for consultation ~16/06/2026) - only press coverage was found; the primary text and consultation deadline on nbs.rs were not located. 3) Official Gazette of RS no. 43/2026, Decision on conditions and manner of establishing and verifying the identity of a natural person using means of electronic communication - the full text, to extract the technical eKYC requirements.
